title: Zhang Zhan — Amnesty Warns Condition Is Life Threatening
summary: Jailed COVID-19 journalist on hunger strike since January 2025. Amnesty calls for immediate release; whereabouts within Shanghai detention unclear since August 2026.
details:
Zhang Zhan, the citizen journalist jailed for reporting from Wuhan in early 2020, is serving a second four-year sentence and Amnesty International describes her condition as life threatening.

HER CONDITION (Amnesty International, May 15, 2026 — ASA 17/1006/2026):
• Serious gastric illness, significant weight loss, extremely weak
• Reportedly on hunger strike against her arbitrary detention since January 2025
• RSF reports she was force-fed and developed stomach complications
• Earlier hunger strikes: August 2021 (11-day hospitalisation) and September 2023

WHERE SHE IS:
• Moved to Zone 5 of Shanghai's Pudong Detention Centre in August 2026, with no update on her health provided (RSF, August 28, 2026)

THE CASE:
• First sentence: 4 years from December 2020 for reporting on the Wuhan outbreak. Released May 13, 2024.
• Re-arrested August 28, 2024, less than four months later.
• Second sentence: 4 years, imposed September 19, 2025 for 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' after a closed-door trial.
• Authorities have persistently refused her a lawyer of her choice, which Amnesty says has hampered efforts to document her situation and appeal her conviction.

WHAT IS BEING ASKED:
• Amnesty International: 'She must be released immediately.' Pending release, she must have access to adequate healthcare provided in compliance with medical ethics.
• RSF: immediate release, and that authorities ensure her safety and access to adequate medical care.

SOURCES:
• Amnesty International: https://www.amnesty.org/en/documents/asa17/1006/2026/en/
• Reporters Without Borders: https://rsf.org/en/two-years-after-her-second-arrest-rsf-outlines-years-long-repression-chinese-journalism-icon-zhang

title: Joshua Wong Pleads Guilty to Foreign Collusion — Awaiting Sentencing
summary: Pleaded guilty at the High Court on September 2, 2026 to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces. Sentencing adjourned with no date set. Faces up to life.
details:
Joshua Wong pleaded guilty on September 2, 2026 at Hong Kong's High Court to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces under the National Security Law. This is his second NSL conviction.

HEARING OUTCOME (September 2, 2026):
• Pleaded guilty to conspiracy to collude with foreign forces
• Judge William Tam adjourned sentencing, saying he would decide "as soon as possible"
• No sentencing date has been set

THE CHARGE:
• Conspiring with Nathan Law (in UK exile, wanted by Hong Kong authorities) and others in 2020 to request that foreign countries impose sanctions, blockades or other hostile measures against the Hong Kong and mainland Chinese governments
• Maximum penalty: LIFE IMPRISONMENT. Foreign collusion carries three to ten years, but ten years becomes the minimum where the offence is found to be of a "grave nature"

WHY THIS MATTERS:
• Wong is already serving four years and eight months for conspiracy to commit subversion in the Hong Kong 47 case
• His lawyer noted he was originally due for release in January 2027 before this case was brought; he will not receive remission on the earlier sentence
• Hong Kong Watch policy director Megan Khoo: the National Security Law "is being weaponised by the Hong Kong authorities to restrict freedom of association, criminalise dissidence" and extend the imprisonment of activists

SOURCES:
• Hong Kong Free Press: https://hongkongfp.com/2026/09/02/breaking-jailed-hong-kong-pro-democracy-campaigner-joshua-wong-pleads-guilty-to-foreign-collusion-charge/
• Hong Kong Watch: https://www.hongkongwatch.org/all-posts/2026/9/2/joshua-wong-joshua-wong-pleads-guilty-in-second-hong-kong-national-security-law-trial
• Al Jazeera: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/2/hong-kong-activist-joshua-wong-pleads-guilty-in-national-security-case

ACTION:
• Share Joshua Wong's case ahead of sentencing
• Contact your representatives to raise his case
• Monitor the sentencing date via Hong Kong Watch and Amnesty International

title: URGENT: Jimmy Lai Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison
summary: Hong Kong media tycoon Jimmy Lai sentenced to 20 years under NSL — confirmed he will not appeal
details:
On December 15, 2025, Jimmy Lai was found guilty on all charges including "conspiracy to collude with foreign forces" under Hong Kong's National Security Law. On February 9, 2026, he was sentenced to 20 years in prison — the harshest sentence yet under the NSL.

As of March 2026, Lai has confirmed he will NOT appeal the conviction (NBC News). The UN has specifically called for his release. Lai, age 78, faces the remainder of his life behind bars.

ACTION NEEDED:
• Contact your representatives to demand his release
• Share his story on social media to raise awareness
• Support the Committee for Freedom in Hong Kong
• Sign petitions calling for sanctions on HK officials

title: 100+ Global Brands Linked to Uyghur Forced Labor
summary: Major investigation identifies over 100 brands in forced labor supply chains; UFLPA entity list now at 144 companies
details:
A joint investigation by The New York Times, The Bureau of Investigative Journalism, and Der Spiegel (May 2025) found over 100 global brands tied to Uyghur forced labor via a Chinese state-imposed labor transfer system. Separately, the US UFLPA Entity List has grown to 144 banned companies (37 added January 2025).

KEY FINDINGS:
• Fashion, technology, automotive, food sectors — Apple, Volkswagen, BMW, Tesla, KFC
• Critical minerals (titanium, lithium, beryllium) supply chains deeply linked
• Estimated 13.75 million labor transfers planned in Xinjiang's current five-year plan
• EU forced labor regulation coming into effect 2027

WHAT YOU CAN DO:
• Check the UFLPA Entity List before making purchases
• Contact companies to demand supply chain transparency
• Support the Coalition to End Forced Labour in the Uyghur Region

title: Hong Kong 47: Appeals Dismissed — Sentences Upheld
summary: Court of Appeal upholds convictions; Amnesty International condemns ruling
details:
The Hong Kong 47 case — the largest prosecution under the National Security Law — saw all 45 activists sentenced to 4-10 years in prison. On February 23, 2026, the Court of Appeal dismissed appeals from 12 defendants, upholding all convictions and sentences.

NOTABLE SENTENCES:
• Benny Tai: 10 years
• Joshua Wong: 4 years 8 months (appeal dismissed Feb 2026)
• Claudia Mo: 4 years 2 months
• Gwyneth Ho: 7 years

Amnesty International called the rejected appeals 'a missed opportunity to start restoring justice.' The ruling confirms Hong Kong's judiciary provides no meaningful check on politically motivated NSL prosecutions.

title: ESCALATION: Family Member Prosecuted Under Article 23
summary: Father of US-based activist sentenced for handling daughter's finances — first family prosecution
details:
On February 26, 2026, Kwok Yin-sang was sentenced to 8 months in prison in Hong Kong for handling the financial assets of his daughter Anna Kwok, a US-based pro-democracy activist and executive director of the Hong Kong Democracy Council.

This marks the FIRST known case of a family member being prosecuted under Article 23 national security provisions for providing financial support to a designated 'absconder.'

WHY THIS MATTERS:
• Sets dangerous precedent — family members are now targets
• Extends transnational repression to relatives who remain in Hong Kong
• Designed to isolate overseas activists by threatening their families
• Could deter Hong Kongers from supporting exiled relatives

ACTION:
• Share this case to raise awareness of Article 23's expanding reach
• Support organizations documenting transnational repression
• Contact representatives about sanctions targeting officials involved
